concept.body: Cavalieri's principle: if two solids share the same height and their cross-sections have equal areas at EVERY level, the volumes are equal — shearing, leaning, or twisting a stack never changes what each level holds. Consequence: oblique prisms and cylinders use V = Bh with the VERTICAL height (never the slant edge).

explanationVariants: Every level of the leaning prism holds the same base-area-10 slice.

widget.prompt: A leaning prism: base area 10, vertical height 6. Volume = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 16 adds — volume is base TIMES height: 60.
30 halves — prisms take the full Bh: 60.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Bh = 60 — identical to its upright twin.

steps.body: Push a stack of coins sideways: it leans, but nothing about any coin changed. **Cavalieri's principle** captures this: if two solids have the same height and their cross-sections at EVERY level have equal areas, their volumes are equal. Volume lives in the slices — how the slices are stacked (straight, sheared, curved) is irrelevant.

explanationVariants: Shearing rearranges the same coins — every level keeps its coin.
Identical volume: the slide moved material sideways, never created or destroyed it.

widget.prompt: Eight identical coins are stacked straight, then pushed into a lean. The leaning stack's volume, compared to the straight stack:

options.label: Exactly equal — every level still holds one full coin of the same area
options.feedback: The figure's shear is volume's alibi: same slices at every height, so Cavalieri certifies the same volume.

options.label: Slightly less — leaning compresses it
options.feedback: The coins never deform — each level keeps its full coin: equal volume.

options.label: Slightly more — it takes up more room
options.feedback: The lean spreads the FOOTPRINT, never the material — slices testify: equal.

options.label: It depends on the lean angle
options.feedback: Any shear, any angle: level-by-level the coins are unchanged — volume is angle-blind.

explanationVariants: Cavalieri compares it to the right prism with the same base and the same VERTICAL height.

widget.prompt: An oblique (leaning) prism has base area 24 and vertical height 7. Its volume = ?

numericErrors.feedback: 31 = 24 + 7 adds — volume multiplies base by height: 168.
84 halves — no halving in prisms: Bh = 168 (Cavalieri matches it to the upright twin).
192 = 24 × 8 sneaks in the SLANT edge — Cavalieri uses the vertical height 7: 168.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Bh = 24 × 7 = 168 — same slices as the upright prism at every level.
widget.successFeedback: Bh = 24 × 7 = 168 — same slices as the upright prism at every level.

explanationVariants: Same story, round base: every level is the same circle of radius 4.

widget.prompt: A leaning cylinder has base radius 4 and vertical height 9. Volume (2 decimals, π ≈ 3.14159) = ?

numericErrors.feedback: 113.1 ≈ 36π uses r = 2 or squares wrong — π(4²)(9) = 144π ≈ 452.39.
226.19 ≈ 72π halves — cylinders take the full Bh: 144π ≈ 452.39.
515.22 pads with extra for the lean — Cavalieri says the lean is free: 144π ≈ 452.39.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: π(16)(9) = 144π ≈ 452.39 — the upright twin's volume exactly.
widget.successFeedback: π(16)(9) = 144π ≈ 452.39 — the upright twin's volume exactly.

predict.prompt: Two solids have equal heights, and their cross-sections match at the bottom and at the top. Must they have the same volume?

options.label: No — they must match at EVERY height, not just two of them
Yes — matching ends is enough to pin the volume
There is no way to tell without the formulas

predict.reveal: No. Cavalieri's hypothesis is every height, and two agreements do not make a theorem — the solids are free to disagree everywhere in between. Sweep the plane through both and hunt for a height where the two readouts come apart.

widget.prompt: Two solids, same height. Sweep the section plane through BOTH and check the areas at matching heights — then stop at the middle.
widget.successFeedback: Equal at every height you tested — THAT is the hypothesis Cavalieri actually needs. Matching at the two ends would have proved nothing; the theorem is about all the slices in between.
widget.positionFeedback: Keep sweeping, then finish at the middle height where both readouts can be compared side by side.
widget.comparisonFeedback: Bring in the second solid. Cavalieri is a comparison theorem — with one solid on screen there is nothing to compare, and 'every cross-section matches' has no second term.
widget.invariantFeedback: Two heights are not 'every height'. Test more before claiming the volumes must agree — that gap is exactly what this lesson is about.

widget.prompt: A deck of cards is a 9-by-6.5 base stacked 4 high (volume 234). It's twisted into a spiral — every card rotated a little. The spiral's volume = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 117 halves — twisting rotates each card in place; every level keeps its full 58.5-area card: 234.
468 doubles — rotation adds nothing: the same 234.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Rotation is a rigid motion of each slice — areas unchanged at every level: 234, by Cavalieri.

hints: Volume needs the VERTICAL height; the problem gives the slant.
The lean shifts the top face 5 sideways while rising vertically — slant, shift, and height make a right triangle.

widget.prompt: A leaning cylinder of radius 2 has a slant edge of length 13, and its top face is shifted 5 units sideways from its base. Volume coefficient (of π) = ?

numericErrors.feedback: 52 = 4 × 13 multiplies by the SLANT — the vertical height is √(13² − 5²) = 12: 48π.
144 forgets to square-then-multiply correctly — r² = 4 and h = 12: 48.
20 = 4 × 5 uses the SHIFT as height — the shift is horizontal; h = 12: 48.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: h = √(169 − 25) = 12; V = π(4)(12) = 48π — Cavalieri charges only vertical height.
widget.successFeedback: h = √(169 − 25) = 12; V = π(4)(12) = 48π — Cavalieri charges only vertical height.

takeaways: Cavalieri: same height + equal cross-sections at EVERY level ⇒ equal volumes.
Oblique prisms and cylinders cost the same as their upright twins — V = Bh with VERTICAL height.
Slant edges are decoys: extract h by Pythagoras before any volume recall.
